chain.label: Recurrent engine and propeller oil leaks on N517SJ
chain.trigger: the engines and propellers had a recent history of oil leaks

chain.label: SAT maintenance never washed the engine compressors after the repeated oil leaks
chain.trigger: there was no record that SAT cleaned the compressors of the engines on N517SJ following any of the incidents

caused_by.evidence: The SAT procedure required the washing of engine compressors 'anytime visible contamination exists, after exposure to prop oil, or compressor contamination is suspected'

chain.label: Oil/tar residue accumulated in the Nos. 1 and 2 compressors and 5th-stage air bleed valves
chain.trigger: All of the internal surfaces and components of the numbers 1 and 2 engine compressors were coated with a tar-like residue

caused_by.evidence: either propeller or engine oil leakage had the potential to cause the degradation of performance indicated in the numbers 1 and 2 engines
the failure of SAT maintenance to clean the engine compressors following oil leaks in the months before the accident allowed the accumulation of oil residues in the engines

chain.label: Training flight flown by a first officer candidate with no L-382/C-130 experience
chain.trigger: the airplane was being flown by a first officer candidate who had no previous L-382/C-130 flight experience

chain.label: Trainee flew an improper landing pitch attitude and mis-flown touchdown
chain.trigger: the captain had been concerned before touchdown that the pitch attitude established by the first officer was incorrect for landing

caused_by.evidence: the captain provided instructional guidance regarding altitude, airplane attitude, airspeed, and power corrections during the approach

chain.label: Captain assumed control and initiated a go-around at touchdown speed (105 KIAS)
chain.trigger: 'Oh, oh, oh. I've got it, I've got it'; he assumed control of the airplane and began a go-around

caused_by.evidence: the captain's initial decision to commence the go-around when he became aware that the airplane was not in a position to properly continue the landing

chain.label: Nos. 1 and 2 engines failed to respond to throttle advance and decelerated about 40 percent rpm
chain.trigger: the number 1 and 2 engines both failed to respond normally, and in fact, decelerated about 40 percent following throttle advancement at the commencement of the go-around

caused_by.evidence: the lack of power section response from the number 1 and 2 engines was directly attributable to the accumulated oil residues in the dirty compressors and air bleed valves
This condition rendered the engines unable to respond to or recover from rapid throttle movement

chain.label: Captain did not promptly recognize the two-engine power loss or the resulting uncontrollability
chain.trigger: the captain either did not recognize promptly that power had been lost from two engines or that the loss of power would potentially render the airplane uncontrollable

caused_by.evidence: The captain had substantial warning that the airplane was experiencing a loss of power from at least one engine, but that information did not become apparent until the go-around had been commenced

chain.label: Flap handle raised during the go-around, contrary to engine-inoperative procedures
chain.trigger: a crewmember said, 'Flaps up.' Apparently in response, the flap handle was raised and flap retraction began

caused_by.evidence: the normal position for the flaps during a landing go-around is 50 percent
a decision which was contrary to engine inoperative emergency procedures

chain.label: Rudder boost pressure reduced from 3,000 to 1,300 psi, cutting available rudder force
chain.trigger: the movement of the flap handle to the retracted position would have reduced rudder boost actuator pressure from 3,000 to 1,300 psi

caused_by.evidence: The consequence of this action would have been a reduction in available rudder force, and a sudden decrease in rudder deflection

chain.label: Captain continued the go-around instead of relanding on the runway
chain.trigger: the captain continued the go-around until control was lost rather than attempting to reland at the first indication that heading and roll control could not be maintained

caused_by.evidence: his continuing the go-around after receiving cues associated with a loss of power from one or more engines must have been influenced by a conviction that the airplane could be flown out of its precarious circumstance

chain.label: Uncontrollable left yaw and roll to about 50 degrees of bank with airspeed decayed to 88 KIAS below Vmca
chain.trigger: Vmca was significantly higher than the actual airspeed and the airplane began an uncontrollable yaw to the left

caused_by.evidence: the number 1 and 2 engine rotor speeds decreased causing substantial thrust asymmetry and increased Vmca
The decision to raise the flaps during the go-around was not only incorrect but it contributed to the cause of the accident by rendering the airplane uncontrollable
The immediate increase of aerodynamic drag further aggravated the controllability problem to preclude the possibility of recovery in the go-around

chain.label: Airplane struck the airfield perimeter fence and impacted the ground left of the runway
chain.trigger: the airplane collided with the airfield perimeter fence in a nose-low and steep left wing low attitude

caused_by.evidence: a left bank at low altitude which steepened until the airplane collided with the airfield perimeter fence

chain.label: All five crewmembers fatally injured; airplane destroyed by impact and postcrash fire
chain.trigger: the airplane was destroyed by ground impact forces and the effects of a postcrash fire. All five crewmen were fatally injured

caused_by.evidence: The causes of death were attributed to multiple traumatic injuries
